system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Global Order: Tech Fractures, Inflation, Wars, Energy
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is in a phase of contested adjustment driven by overlapping shocks: a governance and intelligence crisis in the tech sector that is accelerating US–China decoupling, renewed diplomatic openings amid active wars (Ukraine, Iran-related Gulf tensions) and persistent macro pressure from sticky inflation and tighter monetary policy. These processes interact through markets, supply chains and alliances, producing systemic fragility — volatile asset prices, sharper export controls, and renewed securitisation of critical infrastructure and trade routes. States and firms are re‑routing dependencies while multilateral institutions struggle to reconcile competing security, economic and climate priorities.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and regional security processes; multinational corporations (especially high-tech and energy firms); global financial and commodity markets; critical supply chains (chips, data centres, shipping lanes); international institutions and diplomacy; intelligence, cyber and regulatory interactions that shape trade and investment.
system_description.super_system: The global political-economic system — a world of sovereign states, transnational corporations, integrated markets and planetary ecological constraints.
adjacent_subsystems: Global technology and critical supply chains (semiconductors, data centres, AI ecosystems)
International financial and monetary system (sovereign debt markets, central banks, global investors)
Energy and maritime-security subsystem (Middle East oil flows, shipping lanes, strategic pipelines)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and talks
variables.description: An ongoing high‑intensity conflict between Russia and Ukraine, punctuated by renewed battlefield strikes and intermittent peace talks involving US and other mediators that are shifting the war’s duration and front‑line dynamics.

variables.name: Middle East regional escalation and energy risk
variables.description: Iran‑related hostilities — including Iranian proxies and Houthi strikes against Saudi infrastructure and shipping — are driving episodic attacks on oil and LNG routes, shifting regional escalation risk and global energy market volatility.

variables.name: US–China high‑tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: Strategic competition between the United States and China over semiconductors, AI and related trade controls is accelerating export restrictions, investment frictions and supply‑chain realignment that reshape technological leadership.

variables.name: Global inflation and bond‑market tightening
variables.description: A broad shift toward tighter policy as US and other central banks confront sticky inflation is driving higher sovereign yields, stressed credit conditions and a re‑pricing of financial assets across advanced economies.

variables.name: Transatlantic security realignment
variables.description: Frictions between Washington and European capitals over how to handle Russia and continental defence — from US overtures to calls for European autonomy — are reshaping alliance politics, burden‑sharing and security architecture in Europe.
